hints.title: Boundary Height and Trapping Obstacle
hints.text: Water trapped above bar i equals min(max_left, max_right) - height[i]. Computing these boundary heights for every bar takes quadratic time. How can you find each bar's limiting boundary in a single pass without extra arrays?

hints.title: Smaller Maximum Determines Water
hints.text: If the running maximum on the left is smaller than the running maximum on the right, the left bar's water level is bounded strictly by its left maximum regardless of any taller bars further to the right.

hints.title: Two Pointers with Running Left and Right Maximums
hints.text: Track left and right boundaries alongside left_max and right_max. While left < right, if left_max < right_max, process bar left: add max(0, left_max - height[left]) to the total, update left_max, and increment left. Otherwise process bar right similarly.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of height array (1 <= N <= 2 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Single pass inward with two pointers and two scalar max trackers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Finding left and right maximums independently for each bar with a scan takes O(N^2) time. For N = 2 * 10^4, this requires ~2 * 10^8 operations, which is too slow.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The two-pointer technique achieves O(1) auxiliary space compared to precomputing prefix/suffix arrays which require O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear derivation of water formula min(L_max, R_max) - h[i], reduction from O(N) space prefix arrays to O(1) two pointers, handling empty or monotone inputs.

solutions.approach: Two Pointers with Running Left/Right Max
